question: Should we propose this 3-for-3 to Snow Time Lakers (Kyle): we receive Devin Booker (PHX), Jalen Johnson (ATL) and Donovan Clingan (POR); we send Jamal Murray (DEN), Yaxel Lendeborg (GS) and Isaiah Hartenstein (OKC)? Snow Time Lakers are our matchup 5 opponent (Mon 16 - Sun 22 Nov) and the 48-hour trade review means an accepted deal executes before that week's games. Hartenstein is also in our pending offer to Dr White Slong (Hartenstein + Murphy for RJ Barrett, expires 15 Nov 08:21 UTC); proposing this means withdrawing that one. Kyle's own pending offer (Kyrie + Jalen Johnson for Lendeborg + Murray, expires 15 Nov 09:27 UTC) is the version we would decline.
constraints: The owner's view: Jamal Murray could keep up his current form; Jalen Johnson should improve and get back to 45+ FP/g soon.

The owner's considerations: Jimmy Butler will return (reported January-February 2027, ESPN est. 2 Jan) and it is unclear how that affects Lendeborg's role; Clingan would be another solid player, and the roster has several weak players the owner is happy to rotate; the Suns are winning and Booker is playing better.
The owner's only stated concern is injuries; injury-history research on all six players is in the briefing.

ballots.rationale: The trio we get scored 134.3 FP/g in 2026 (Johnson 53.1/72 GP, Clingan 41.0/77, Booker 40.2/64) against about 123 for ours. We sell at peak: Murray's L7 55.7 (3) is a shooting spike, Lendeborg's 44.5 rate comes while Curry is out (ESPN est. 12 Dec) and before Butler (ESPN est. 2 Jan) and Moody (ESPN est. 1 Dec) return. We buy Johnson at a trough with a known cause (L15 33.8 (4), ankle sprain, 20.5% 3P). The cost is matchup 5 against Kyle: with Johnson's form-table rate it goes from about +69 to about -74, roughly 0.3 wins. Against that I estimate about +6 FP/g, roughly 21 FP a week, over weeks 6-20, worth about +0.7 wins plus a playoff-week edge.

ballots.rationale: On non-thin samples the three we get total 134.4 FP/g on 2026 lines over 64, 72 and 77 games, against 123.2 to 127.2 for what we send (Murray 47.8 over 75, Hartenstein 34.01 over 47, Lendeborg 41.4/45.4 on 12 games, NO_SAMPLE in the CSV), so +7 to +11. Two pairs hold on every measure: Booker 41.5 (11) vs Lendeborg 41.4 (12), and Clingan +4.0 to +7.0 over Hartenstein with 77 vs 47 games played last season. The No case is Johnson vs Murray on 9-10 games: Murray's 54.7 (9) is 6.9 above his 75-game line, and Johnson's 42.3 (9) is 10.8 below his 72-game 53.08 on 20.5% from three. The Rate's -12.8 is built almost entirely on those THIN windows.

ballots.rationale: Availability is a wash: at my estimates the six project to about 165 games for the side we send and 166 for the side we get over the about 66 remaining team games, so the owner's injury worry is not what this deal buys. It swaps Hartenstein's recurring calf (47/82 last season) for Clingan's durability (88 of 93 since 2025-26), but takes on Jalen Johnson's record (36/82 in 2024-25 with a season-ending labrum tear, 9/12 now) and Booker's December groin pattern. Multiplying FP/g by chance of playing, we send 111.2 per team game and get 100.0 on the Rate (−5.0 using ESPN's P_GP), and Johnson needs about 54 FP/g, above his 53.1 in 2026, to break even. It also hands Kyle about 100 FP in matchup 5 against us (495 vs 395 at the Rate, 11 player-games vs 10), a swing of about 200 FP in that head-to-head.

ballots.rationale: On role, we sell Lendeborg at his largest role: 31.0 min and 37.1 FP/g in the 9 full games Curry played, against 35.3 min and 54.3 FP/g in the 3 without him. Curry (ESPN est. 12 Dec), Moody (ESPN est. 1 Dec) and Butler (ESPN est. 2 Jan) are all due back, and no team statement covers his role after that. Johnson (37.0 L7 min against 35.21 last season) and Clingan are back in their 2026 roles and producing 10.8 and 3.4 FP/g below their 2026 numbers, so the gap is shooting, not opportunity. Murray's role is the same as last season and his number holds, so losing him is the real cost and only partly offset. The deal is -12.8 FP/g by Rate but +18.8 on 2026 numbers, and I expect it to come out positive over the rest of the season.
